thread:
Ivy: Observing more billing noise: some service-account keys are billed to the org root instead of the creating project. We should formalize routing precedence.
Samir: Agreed. Current order (principal -> key) is causing surprises when long-lived keys are used across projects.
Rohit: Proposal: canonical precedence: 1) explicit exchange header (if auth check passed), 2) key.created_project (if present), 3) principal-inferred project, 4) tenant default.
Kayla: UI/Policy note: communicate change in key detail: show "Billing source: project X (from key)" with link to docs. Allow org admins to opt into legacy behavior via tenant setting.
Ivy: Telemetry: emit routing.project_resolution_total{source="exchange|key|principal|fallback"} and billing.attribution_diff_counter when billed project != key.created_project. Keep labels low-cardinality.
sre-bot: created alert routing-project-mismatch-high if billing.attribution_diff_counter > 0.5% sustained 10m
Samir: Rollout plan: feature-flag the routing change, start canary at 0.5% traffic, run backfill to populate key.created_project for historical keys (dry-run first), warm cache, then increase to 5/25/100%.
Rohit: Backfill caveats: do not overwrite existing created_project; mark ambiguous results for manual review. Use DB transactional writes and a migration lock.
Kayla: UX: add filter "billing source != key project" in keys list and a bulk-assign action for admins. Copy: "This key was billed to a different project than its creator. Review exchange policies or reassign the key."
Ivy: I'll open RFC + tickets: auth change, gateway cache update, backfill job, UI work, dashboards + alerts. Target first canary next Tuesday.
